**Synopsis:**
Rooftop solar adoption in Great Britain is accelerating, driven by rising wholesale electricity prices and falling installation costs. Even in the UK's cloudiest regions, a standard 4kW south-facing system can save households ~£450/year; southern regions up to £618/year. Solar supplied a record 14.4% of GB electricity in July, boosted by climate-intensified heatwaves. Growth is structural: Labour's 2030 solar tripling target, record H1 installations, and new plug-in balcony panels broadening access. Affordability (~£7,000 upfront) remains a barrier, but demand is structurally rising.
